title: Transport along the pullback preserves K-flat complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of
schemes. The transport
$\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})\colon\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}\to\Mod_{f^*\Lambda_Y}$ along
the strong monoidal pullback of abelian sheaves ([sk-def-sfb-transport],
[def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal]) sends K-flat complexes ([sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]) of
$\Lambda_Y$-modules to K-flat complexes of $f^*\Lambda_Y$-modules, for the relative
tensor products of [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor].

proof.text: Put $R=\Lambda_Y$ and $S=f^*_{\mathrm{Ab}}R$. For each of the two pro-etale sites, the tensor on abelian sheaves is the sheafified objectwise tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Apply [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] to $R$ and $S$: its equivalences $E_R,E_S$ identify internal modules with sectionwise module sheaves, identify their direct-sum total relative tensors, and preserve and reflect K-flatness. Thus for a K-flat internal complex $P$, $E_RP$ is K-flat over the section-ring sheaf $R_{\mathrm{sec}}$. It remains to prove K-flatness of $E_S\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\mathrm{Ab}})P$.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; internal/sectionwise comparison as stated in lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison

proof.text: Write $u=f_{\mathrm{proet}}$ for the geometric morphism of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Its abelian inverse image is the sheafified left Kan extension defining $f^*_{\mathrm{Ab}}$, and its strong monoidal structure is [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal]. Under the equivalences in step 1, $S_{\mathrm{sec}}=u^{-1}R_{\mathrm{sec}}$ canonically, and the transported module is $u^{-1}(E_RP)$ with its induced module action. Indeed [sk-def-sfb-transport] gives the action $f^*R\otimes f^*M\to f^*(R\otimes M)\to f^*M$. Evaluating on local pure tensors makes this the action obtained by applying $u^{-1}$ to the bilinear scalar action; the unit and multiplication are the images of the original unit and multiplication in exactly the same way. The identifications leave the underlying inverse-image abelian sheaf and maps unchanged, hence also identify each differential of the two termwise complexes. This proves the identification on complexes, not only on objects.

source.place: Proof, opening identification with module inverse image; action formula expanded from sk-def-sfb-transport(1)

proof.text: Let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}})$ be any topos point and let $q=u\circ p$. By [def-trf-geometric-morphism], this is a point of $\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\mathrm{proet}})$ and $q^{-1}=p^{-1}u^{-1}$. The forward implication of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-kflat-stalk-criterion] applied to $E_RP$ says that $(E_RP)_q$ is K-flat over $(R_{\mathrm{sec}})_q$. Step 2 and the composite inverse-image formula give $(E_S\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\mathrm{Ab}})P)_p\cong(E_RP)_q$ over $(S_{\mathrm{sec}})_p\cong(R_{\mathrm{sec}})_q$. The action agrees because both are $p^{-1}u^{-1}$ of the original action; the differentials agree because both are $p^{-1}u^{-1}d_P$. Consequently the target stalk complex is K-flat. This uses no extension to a different stalk ring.

source.place: Tag 0DEN, lemma-check-K-flat-stalks (1); compare the pointwise proof of Tag 0DEP, lemma-pullback-K-flat-points

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-proetale-enough-points], the small pro-etale topos of $X$ admits a set-indexed conservative family of topos points. Step 3 gives K-flatness at every member of this family. Apply the reverse implication of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-kflat-stalk-criterion] on $X$ to conclude that $E_S\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\mathrm{Ab}})P$ is K-flat. Finally [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] reflects K-flatness through $E_S$, giving the required K-flatness for the internal relative tensor product. In particular the argument tests every acyclic $S$-module complex on $X$, through the converse stalk criterion, rather than just complexes pulled back from $Y$.
